doc.title: Greg Caputo interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, March 14, 1998

title: The 1963 Brubeck Carnegie Hall concert he would attend
summary: Given a time machine, he would hear the Brubeck Quartet's 1963 Carnegie Hall concert and Morello's drum solo.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Charlie Parker: encounters, lore and legacy

blocks.x: Do you ever look back in time, speaking of Americana, if you could go back in a time machine, would there be an era that you would prefer or be interested in living in?

There is a specific concert that I would love to attend, but to go back to the big band era, like during World War II, I think when they were at their height I think. I would love to go back and spend a couple of years and listen, and that would be great to experience that, to meet some of these people and talk with them, to experience the Carnegie Hall

concert. But there’s definitely one concert, in 1963 there was a concert, in November, that the Dave Brubeck Quartet performed. And it was a legendary concert. And it is out on a double CD right now, where everybody was just at their prime and swinging and the group had never really reached heights like that before and it was recorded. And probably the most phenomenal drum solo ever performed was done at that concert, and I would like to have observed that.
Was that at a college in the midwest or something?

It was at Carnegie Hall. At the time the newspapers were on strike and they didn’t think there was going to be anyone there. It was sold out. And when they walked out there, just the sound of the hall and the sold out audience, everybody played phenomenal. Joe Morello had the flu, and how he ever pulled off this, what I only can say as far as I’m concerned, the greatest drum solo ever played, I would have liked to have been there for that.
Much like an athlete, just reach down and pulled out that, whatever Muhammad Ali had.
And he is, he’s up there with those people. It was a phenomenal concert. I would have liked to have been there. I think every musician would have a concert they’re after.
